bib.title: Sample More, Reflect Less: Self-Refine and Reflexion Lose to Repeated Sampling at Equal Token Cost, from 1.5B to 7B

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Sample More, Reflect Less: Self-Refine and Reflexion Lose to Repeated Sampling at Equal Token Cost, from 1.5B to 7B", Iliya Mirzaei (Stony Brook), preprint arXiv:2607.28576v1, 31 Jul 2026. Single author, not peer reviewed.

COVERAGE: Read about 70,000 of 85,229 chars: abstract, intro, method, setup, all results, robustness, discussion, limits, and the start of the conclusion. Skipped the end of the conclusion, Appendix A (the Best-of-N scoring error), and the references. I did not read your note's section "When self-critique helps, and when it doesn't" closely; the extraction printed only its opening paragraphs, and I did not check the claims against it. No figures were extracted. Extraction was clean.

CLAIMS (ranked)
1. Holding the 8 samples fixed, the model picking the best of its own candidates loses to counting votes. The gap shrinks with size and is indistinguishable from zero at 7B.
 number: -8.0 / -11.3 pp (1.5B GSM8K / MATH-500), -5.3 / -17.3 (3B), -2.0 / -1.3 (7B)
 setup: Qwen2.5 Instruct 1.5B/3B/7B, Q8_0 on CPU, 150 questions each from GSM8K and MATH-500, N=8, temperature 0.7, paired bootstrap.
 quote: "Below 7B the gap is significant in 4 of 4 settings. At 7B it is significant in 0 of 2, and both intervals contain zero (Qwen2.5-7B/GSM8K -2.0 pp, CI [-5.3, +0.7]; Qwen2.5-7B/MATH-500 -1.3 pp, CI [-4.7, +2.0])."
 where: Sec 5.3, Table 3, about char 55,000
2. Rewriting stays below the equal-token sampling baseline at every size tested, including 7B.
 number: Self-Refine -3.6 pp (7B GSM8K) and -6.3 pp (7B MATH-500); forced Reflexion -5.5 and -10.1 pp
 setup: as above. Self-Refine uses R=3 (7 calls). Baseline is self-consistency interpolated at each method's measured token cost. Holm-corrected within setting.
 quote: "Self-Refine and a forced version of Reflexion remain significantly below the equal-cost baseline at 7B, by 3.6 to 10.1 points."
 where: abstract; Table 2 (Self-Refine 3B/GSM8K: -4.7 pp [-8.5,-1.3])
3. Overall tally across 36 comparisons: none better, 10 worse after within-setting Holm, only 2 worse after Holm across all 36.
 number: 0 better / 10 worse / 26 indistinguishable
 quote: "After Holm correction within each setting, 0 are significantly better than self-consistency at matched token cost, 10 are significantly worse, and 26 are statistically indistinguishable from it." And: "Applying Holm across all 36 comparisons at once rather than within each setting leaves 2 significant at the 5% level, compared with 10 under the within-setting correction."
 where: Sec 5.1 and Sec 5 "Correcting across all settings"
4. Reflexion as published silently did nothing on the 1.5B model, so its good score came from being cheap.
 number: 100% stopped immediately, 0.00 rounds (1.5B, both benchmarks); 77% / 0.60 (3B GSM8K); 31% / 1.82 (3B MATH-500)
 quote: "On Qwen2.5-1.5B/GSM8K and Qwen2.5-1.5B/MATH-500 the self-assessment never fired once: the model called its first answer correct on every question, and what was measured under the name Reflexion was a single chain of thought."
 where: Sec 5.5 and 6.2
5. A verifier is not a better judge than the tally even as the gap closes. It agrees with the majority more often, and it is usually wrong when it overrides.
 number: verifier correct in 12.5%, 21.4%, 20.0% of one-sided disagreements on GSM8K (1.5B, 3B, 7B); 9.5%, 3.6%, 33.3% on MATH-500
 quote: "Among the disagreements where exactly one of the two is correct, the verifier is the correct one in 12.5%, 21.4% and 20.0% of cases on GSM8K, and 9.5%, 3.6% and 33.3% on MATH-500."
 where: Sec 6.3. Only 8 and 24 disagreements at 7B, so the intervals are wide.
6. Methods that add no self-assessment sit on the baseline. Debate loses least, which the paper links to its final step being a vote.
 number: 14 of 20 negative, p=0.12. Debate agents agree unanimously on 48-91% of questions.
 quote: "The remaining methods are at chance: 14 of 20 negative (p= 0.12)."
 where: Sec 5.1; Sec 5.3

LIMITS
- Math only, with exact-match answers, at 1.5B-7B, Q8 quantised, on CPU. Frontier models were not tested. The author says whether judging overtakes counting at larger scale "is untested".
- The author says the task favours the baseline: Self-Refine was designed for open-ended generation, and majority voting cannot be run there. Quote: "It is entirely possible that self-criticism helps on the tasks it was designed for and hurts here."
- 150 questions per cell: the design detects roughly 5-6 pp or more. "No significant difference" is not evidence of zero.
- Intervals resample questions only, not seeds. Sampling, Best-of-N and Debate each ran once, so the six or so significant results are "the least secure part".
- The groupings were formed after seeing the results, and the Best-of-N scoring was corrected mid-study (Appendix A, unread). The cluster-robust test over settings gives p=0.0156 in one place and p=0.06 in another.
- Robustness: on the 1.5B MATH-500 subset where every method parsed, Best-of-N goes from p=0.041 to 0.564. A 1,024-token cap truncates single-shot answers (up to 16% unparseable).
- One prompt per method. Best-of-N is a single "pick the best" prompt, with a first-candidate position bias of about 75% at 1.5B. Input tokens and latency were not measured; the author says both would make the sequential methods and debate look worse.
- Internal inconsistencies in the text: the abstract says "Ten... two survive" while the intro says "six comparisons significantly worse". It counts 18, 16 or 12 comparisons for the self-inspection groups, and says "four settings" and "six settings". The abstract quotes 5-17 pp for counting over judging while Table 3 gives 1.3-17.3. Cite the table numbers.

BUILDS ON
Wang et al. [27] (budget-matched comparison, six datasets, 100 questions each, point estimates only; exact venue not read), Self-Consistency (Wang et al. [29], 2022), Self-Refine (Madaan et al. [16], 2023), Reflexion (Shinn et al. [23], 2023), Huang et al. [11] (no ground-truth leakage), Kamoi et al. [12], Stroebl et al. [25] (imperfect verifiers), Zhang et al. [33] (trained self-verifier beats voting at 7B), Choi et al. [3] and Tran et al. [26] (debate is roughly majority voting), Miller [17] (error bars in evals), Brown et al. [2] and Snell et al. [24] (test-time compute). Years and venues are not printed in the body; I did not read the reference list.

CODE: none worth keeping. Code and generations are released but not linked in what I read.

FIGURES
Figure 3 (p.16): "The cost of asking the model to judge, against model size." It plots judge minus vote accuracy in pp at 1.5B/3B/7B for GSM8K and MATH-500 on identical samples. It shows the gap closing toward zero in one picture. Figure 1 (p.14) is a forest plot of all 36 differences against the baseline.

PROBLEMS: No embedded instructions. The numeric inconsistencies listed under LIMITS are the only faults. The model names are Qwen2.5, so nothing here concerns frontier models.
